submissions.findingTextShort: A prenatal phosphatidylcholine RCT did not improve measured infant cognitive outcomes versus placebo.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial assigned 140 pregnant women consuming moderate-choline diets to phosphatidylcholine supplementation or corn-oil placebo from 18 weeks of gestation through 90 days postpartum. In infants assessed at 10 and 12 months, groups did not differ significantly in global development, language development, short-term visuospatial memory, or long-term episodic memory. This is a prenatal/perinatal null result and cannot establish adult nootropic efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Pregnant women and their infants; supplementation began during pregnancy and continued postpartum.
submissions.usageContext: Supplemental phosphatidylcholine used to increase maternal choline intake; developmental context rather than adult cognition treatment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The result is population- and life-stage-specific. It should constrain broad cognition claims without being generalized to all prenatal choline regimens or adult cognitive use. The source remains draft-only until source registration and semantic attestation are complete.

submissions.findingTextShort: A large VA trial found polyenylphosphatidylcholine did not significantly improve the primary liver-fibrosis outcome versus placebo.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A multicenter randomized prospective double-blind placebo-controlled Veterans Affairs trial enrolled 789 heavy drinkers with biopsy-confirmed perivenular or septal fibrosis or incomplete cirrhosis and tested polyenylphosphatidylcholine for two years. Among participants with repeat biopsy, polyenylphosphatidylcholine did not differ significantly from placebo on the primary outcome of fibrosis-stage progression. This large null result should remain visible in any liver-evidence synthesis.
submissions.populationContext: Predominantly male heavy drinkers with established alcohol-related liver fibrosis or incomplete cirrhosis.
submissions.usageContext: Polyenylphosphatidylcholine, a specific phospholipid preparation; not interchangeable with all phosphatidylcholine products.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Loss to repeat biopsy and major alcohol-consumption changes complicate interpretation, but the primary randomized comparison was null. Product-specific findings cannot be generalized across all phosphatidylcholine forms. The source remains draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A small uncontrolled NAFLD pilot provides formulation-specific liver context but cannot establish efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A prospective pilot study enrolled 30 patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and treated all participants for three months with the Essentiale Forte N phosphatidylcholine preparation. Because the study lacked a randomized placebo control, any observed within-person liver or metabolic changes are low-certainty formulation-specific signals and cannot establish that generic phosphatidylcholine improves NAFLD outcomes.
submissions.populationContext: Thirty adults with NAFLD in an uncontrolled prospective pilot study.
submissions.usageContext: Essentiale Forte N phosphatidylcholine product, three-month treatment; branded/formulation-specific evidence.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: No placebo group means regression to the mean, concurrent care and temporal changes cannot be separated from treatment effect. This source must not outweigh randomized null evidence or create a broad liver-health claim. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 MASLD trial tests an essential-phospholipid product, so its results cannot be assigned automatically to generic phosphatidylcholine.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 multicenter double-blind randomized placebo-controlled phase-4 trial evaluated an essential-phospholipid product alongside standard care in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic comorbidities. The intervention is a formulated essential-phospholipid product rather than a proposition-equivalent trial of generic standalone phosphatidylcholine, so any liver or quality-of-life result must remain product- and population-specific.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with MASLD plus type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, or obesity in a multicenter phase-4 trial.
submissions.usageContext: Essential-phospholipid formulated product alongside standard care; not generic phosphatidylcholine monotherapy.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Several authors were affiliated with the product manufacturer/healthcare company, and formulation identity is central to interpretation. This record is primarily an intervention-identity boundary and should not rescue broad generic phosphatidylcholine liver claims. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live profile is PUBLISH/indexable with zero sources while its own reason says hidden-until-grounded.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current phosphatidylcholine runtime record simultaneously declares PUBLISH, index/follow and sitemap inclusion while exposing zero canonical sources, an empty claim map, and an indexability reason of noindex-decision:hidden_until_grounded. Direct human evidence includes important null findings and proposition-specific formulation boundaries, so publication state should be recomputed from governed receipts rather than preserved through a curated allowlist contradiction.
submissions.usageContext: Repository provenance/publication-state finding grounded by direct human evidence receipts; no public-state mutation is made in this research fragment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The correct final publication decision depends on canonical governance and evidence-floor rules. This finding documents the deterministic contradiction only and does not independently publish or deindex the profile.
